text:
alex: Quick heads-up — I want to bump the prefix-cache key schema (v1 -> v2) to include model_variant and a quantized boolean. Before I open the PR: is there any contract we expose to customers that would cause a breaking change?

maria: Good call pinging this. Current stable headers we document are `x-prefix-cache-hit` and `x-prefix-cache-ttl`. We don't publish the key schema itself. If we add a header like `x-prefix-key-schema: v2` that's backwards-compatible. Do we need to change the hit semantics?

simon: Streaming note: right now the cache hit header only appears on the final HTTP response. If downstreams expect the header earlier (or inside event stream), that could confuse clients. Do we plan to emit a streaming event like `event: cache_hit`?

alex: My intent is to keep `x-prefix-cache-hit` semantics exactly the same (true/false). Add `x-prefix-key-schema: v2` and `x-prefix-cache-key-meta: model=...;quantized=1` for debug only. No behavior changes to hits.

rachel: Invalidation question — when a model is rotated (e.g., model_id changes or quantization toggled), v2 keys will no longer match v1. How do we want to handle TTL vs explicit invalidation? We should avoid leaving stale v1 keys that continue to be served to Dedicated customers.
maria: Proposed migration plan: 1) servers accept both v1 and v2 keys for reads for 14 days, 2) write new requests as v2, 3) emit both `x-prefix-key-schema` and `x-prefix-cache-hit` so ops can see migration impact, 4) after 14d flip to v2-only.
simon: Example response headers I propose (HTTP):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-prefix-cache-hit: true
x-prefix-key-schema: v2
x-prefix-cache-ttl: 120
x-prefix-cache-key-meta: model=redwood-7b,quantized=1
```

That keeps `x-prefix-cache-hit` unchanged. Clients that ignore `x-prefix-key-schema` keep working.

alex: Sounds reasonable. A couple follow-ups: 1) for streaming/gRPC should we send the schema as the first chunk? 2) Is there any downstream (analytics, billing) that depends on the shape of the key?
maria: For streaming, let's include a one-line `:meta x-prefix-key-schema=v2` control event as the first message on stream so SDKs can opt-in. For analytics/billing — AFAIK no system parses the key itself, they only look at the header. But tag rollout to infra-team to double-check.
rachel: Ops checklist: add a rollout metric `prefix_cache_hit_rate_v2` and alert if >5% drop vs baseline. Also add an explicit invalidation endpoint we can call for Dedicated when we flip quantization settings.
simon: I'll drop a small code example in the PR showing new key composition (pseudo):

```
// prefix-cache key v2
key = sha256(prefix + "|" + model_id + "|" + (quantized ? "q1" : "q0"))
// keep existing namespace so we can attempt best-effort lookup of v1 keys
```
deploy-bot: Staging rollout scheduled: 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC — will deploy feature flag `prefix_key_v2` to 20% in staging.

alex: I'm going to open the PR with the migration plan + feature flag + docs changes. Please review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321 (draft). Looking for quick LGTM from @maria and @rachel and someone to own rollout monitoring.
maria: LGTM from docs/contract perspective. Please add a small unit test that asserts header presence for both streaming and non-streaming paths.
rachel: LGTM on ops side but add rollback steps to the PR (how to revert feature flag + invalidate v2 writes). I'll coordinate the invalidation runbook.
simon: I'll own the rollout monitoring and dashboards. Happy to help with tests. Ping me in PR for review.
alex: Thanks all — merging to draft shortly. If anyone spots a customer-facing backward-compat issue call it out here. :thumbsup:
